records.name: Pennsport Civic Association
records.summary: Neighbors in Pennsport who meet most months with city and state officials to hear about zoning and building projects. The group also runs neighborhood cleanups and park volunteer days.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over. Members can also join the cleanups and park volunteer days.

schedule.text: General membership meetings on the second Wednesday of each month at 7 pm, except July and August.

first_step.how: Come to the second Wednesday general meeting at 7 pm at EOM Athletic Association, 144 Moore St. There is no meeting in July or August.
first_step.basis: The group's site says in-person attendance is the best way to take part and that anyone who lives in Pennsport counts as a member. No sign-up step is listed, but the site does not say newcomers are specially welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings are held in the hall at EOM Athletic Association on Moore Street. Recent meetings covered updates from city and state offices, utility construction work, and zoning variance requests, so you can listen before you speak. The site does not say how long a meeting runs.
first_visit_tips: Plan around the summer break, since there are no meetings in July or August.
Come in person, because the group says that is the best way to take part.

records.notes: Meeting schedule and venue come from pennsport.org and its meetings page. The May 2026 forum on the homepage is the newest dated item with a year. Undated September items on the homepage were not used. The email is now the address the group publishes on its contact page; the City list email was a different address. The site names no phone number or contact person, so the City list phone and contact name are kept. Partner groups named on the site are in leads_only.

records.name: Philadelphia Stories
records.summary: A nonprofit that publishes a free literary magazine every quarter and runs writing masterclasses, contests and readings for writers and readers in the Philadelphia area.
records.what_you_do: Read the free magazine or sign up for the newsletter. Writers who live in or come from Pennsylvania, Delaware or New Jersey can submit fiction, poetry, nonfiction or art. You can also take a paid masterclass in novel writing or poetry. A pitch event called Pitch Fest is planned for 2027.

schedule.text: Online masterclasses in novel writing and poetry, each booked through its own ticket page.

locations.label: Mailing address (IRS record; the site lists no office)

cost.text: The magazine is free to read. Masterclasses are paid and booked through ticket links, with prices shown on those ticket pages.

first_step.how: Download a free issue from philadelphiastories.org or subscribe to the newsletter. If you want to submit work, read the submission guidelines first.
first_step.basis: Anyone can read the free magazine and subscribe to the newsletter, and the site gives a clear route for writers to submit. There is no in-person visit, and masterclasses are paid.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site has no in-person visit to plan for. The magazine is free to download, and submissions have no reading fee. Paid online masterclasses in novel writing and poetry are booked through separate ticket pages.
first_visit_tips: Read the submission guidelines before you send work, since submissions are open to writers and artists who live in, grew up in, or have lived in PA, DE or NJ.
The window for the Winter/Spring 2027 issue opens November 15, 2026 and closes February 1, 2027, as the page prints it.

records.notes: No office or in-person events are listed. The events section says coming soon, so no event dates are recorded. The mailing address comes from IRS records because the site publishes no address; the 'Stret' typo is corrected to 'Street'. Masterclass prices are not on the site. Pitch Fest dates are not posted. PS Junior (ages 18 and under) is a youth program on the site and is not recorded separately.

records.name: Point Breeze Community Development Coalition
records.summary: A community group for Point Breeze in South Philadelphia. It holds a monthly meeting, runs committees on housing, jobs, safety, quality of life and youth, and is a City registered community organization that talks over zoning and development plans.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over. Pick a committee on housing and land use, business and jobs, safety, quality of life, history and culture, youth services, or community organizing and advocacy.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the third Friday at 9 am, held with Point Breeze Community Network Plus.

first_step.how: Come to the monthly meeting at 9 am on the third Friday at 1350 Capitol Street, or email pbcdcoalition@gmail.com to ask about joining a committee.
first_step.basis: The home page welcomes new residents, and the Get Involved page names the monthly meeting, seven committees and an email address for questions. It does not describe a sign-up process.
first_step.what_to_expect: The monthly meeting is a morning session at 9 am on the third Friday, held with Point Breeze Community Network Plus. You can pick a committee that fits your interests, such as housing, jobs or safety. The site does not give the meeting length, the agenda, or any membership fee.
first_visit_tips: The site lists no meeting dates for the year, so check Facebook or email the group to confirm the next one.

records.notes: The site shows no dated posts. Its only year is a 2023 footer copyright, which is not used as evidence. Status is probably_active because the site works but shows no dates; the last sign of life is the City RCO list. The meeting place comes from the Get Involved page, which does not print a city, so Philadelphia was added. The old 'Meeting place' sentence is replaced with this address. The email is now the address the group publishes; the City list had a different address. Point Breeze Community Network Plus is named as co-host and is in leads_only.

records.summary: A neighborhood group the City of Philadelphia has registered to be consulted on zoning and development in the South part of the city, Residents Organized for Advocacy and Direction gives neighbors a place to hear about projects and respond.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over.

locations.label: Meeting place (City list)
locations.address: Zion Hill Memorial Baptist Church, 2702 Ellsworth Street, Philadelphia, PA 19146

first_step.how: Call or email the contact listed here and ask for the next meeting date and place.
first_step.basis: The only web page listed for the group is on Facebook, and no meeting time or sign-up step appears on any public site we could check, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The only web presence is a Facebook page. Facebook is a lead-only platform, so it was not read for facts. One web search found no other public page for this group, so the site had no more detail than tier 1. Status is probably_active: the group is on the City registry, but no dated activity was found on a public site. The meeting place is from the City list, with 'Phila' written out as Philadelphia.

records.name: South Broad Street Neighborhood Association
records.summary: Neighbors around South Broad Street who meet most months to talk over zoning and building plans. The group also runs a few community events, such as a fall pumpkin carve.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over. Zoning meetings are held on Zoom.

schedule.text: Meetings most months at 7 pm, usually posted a few days ahead. Some months, including several summer months, have no meeting.

locations.label: Meeting place (City list)
locations.address: 1930 South Broad St, Philadelphia, PA (Constitution Health Plaza)

first_step.how: Fill in the join form on sbsna.org (name, address and email), then watch for the next meeting post and register through its Zoom link if the meeting is online.
first_step.basis: Meetings are open, and the site has a clear join form and an email list. Meeting dates are posted only a few days ahead, and zoning meetings need a Zoom registration.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings usually start at 7 pm and cover zoning and building plans for the area. Zoning meetings are held on Zoom, and the site asks attendees to register through the link on the meeting post. The site does not say how long meetings run or what they cost, and it lists no dues.
first_visit_tips: Check the site a few days before, since some months have no meeting.
Register through the Zoom link on the meeting post if you plan to join online.

records.notes: The site names no physical meeting place. The Constitution Health Plaza address is from the City list and is kept. The phone number is from the City list only, since the site publishes none. The Tuesday weekday is derived from the posted meeting dates, which all fell on a Tuesday; the site does not state it. The contact name and email match the Zoning Chair listed on the contacts page.

records.name: South of South Neighborhood Association (SOSNA)
records.summary: Volunteer neighbors for the Graduate Hospital area, between Broad Street and the Schuylkill River and between Washington Avenue and South Street. Members vote for the board, join committees on zoning, clean and green, Vision Zero street safety, and economic development, and work on street trees.
records.what_you_do: Join a committee (Economic Development, Clean and Green, Vision Zero, Zoning, SOSNA Impact outreach, or Triangles), report empty tree pits, or run for the board.

locations.label: General member voting meeting (Christian St. YMCA Annex)
Address on City list
locations.address: 1901 Washington Ave., Unit B, Philadelphia, PA 19146

cost.text: Membership is free, with no dues or donation required.

first_step.how: Come to the October 15 general member voting meeting at the Christian St. YMCA Annex, 1724 Christian St., 6:30 to 8:30 pm. Anyone can attend.
first_step.basis: Meetings are open to everyone, and joining is a free online form. Voting is limited to members who live, own property or run a business in the area, so there is a clear way in for the public.
first_step.what_to_expect: The fall general member voting meeting is a two-hour evening session at the Christian Street YMCA Annex. Members vote for board seats at this meeting. Board nominations close online on Sunday, October 11, 2026, and self-nominees go on the ballot automatically.
first_visit_tips: Joining online takes a few minutes: you confirm your email with a six-digit code, then give your address and your connection to the neighborhood.

Only members vote. Residents, property owners, businesses and nonprofits headquartered in the area get full votes; people who live outside the area can join as associates and take part without voting.

records.notes: The October 15 meeting date is printed without a year. The 2026 evidence is the nomination deadline, Sunday, October 11, 2026, printed on the board elections page. Membership is free according to the join page. The committees page URL is misspelled on the site (commitees); it is cited as written and not used for other facts. A 2025 Board Nominations link has a 2024 URL, so it was not used as evidence. The calendar page lists no events, only the iCal feed.

records.name: South Philadelphia Communities Civic Association (SPCCA)
records.summary: South Philadelphia Communities Civic Association (SPCCA) is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the South part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

first_step.how: Email the contact listed here and ask for the next meeting date and place.
